notes: Connection reuse, and nothing else. Arm A is the current behaviour exactly - a client built, used once and closed, so every request pays DNS, TCP and TLS. Arm B takes one client from a pool and leaves it open. The request itself is byte identical between them: same claude-sonnet-5, same six frozen packets, same benchmark system prompt, same 220-token cap, no thinking, no output_config, no TTS, and the 25-word production chunk rule untouched. Arm B pins a 300s keep-alive because the SDK expires an idle connection after 5s and the harness alternates arms - without it the reuse arm would silently reconnect every trial and the experiment would measure nothing. So arm B is 'one client, kept alive', which is the intervention a production change would actually make. Every trial records whether the connection was really reused, so a failed arm shows as a failed arm.
